title: In Conversation: Founder James on the Plateau Nobody Warns You About
dek: You can order dinner, joke with a taxi driver, read a novel — and still feel like you have stopped improving. Founder James (JY DM) explains why the B1–B2 plateau is not a failure of talent, why ‘more of the same’ keeps you stuck, and how this month’s issue is built to break the loop.

blocks.text: September is when adults go back to studying. The notebooks come out, the app streaks restart, and the same quiet disappointment arrives a few weeks later: the words are there, the grammar is there, and yet every conversation sounds exactly like last year’s conversation. Learners call this stagnation. COSYmagazine calls it the plateau — and this entire issue is dedicated to it. We sat down with founder James (JY DM) to ask what the plateau actually is, why the usual advice makes it worse, and how the articles in this volume are designed to move a B1 speaker into B2 territory.
blocks.say: September is when adults go back to studying. The notebooks come out, the app streaks restart, and the same quiet disappointment arrives a few weeks later. Learners call this stagnation. We call it the plateau, and this entire issue is dedicated to it.

blocks.text: This Month: Me vs the Intermediate Plateau
blocks.say: This Month: Me vs the Intermediate Plateau

blocks.text: Before we begin, a word about the issue itself. Vol. 2026.09 is built around a single diagnosis: intermediate learners do not lack vocabulary, they lack range. So the issue attacks range from four directions. The Words desk gives you fifty conversational upgrades for the phrases you already overuse, and fifty stronger adjectives to replace ‘very’. A second Words piece takes the ten most worn-out verbs and hands you precise synonyms. And the Long Read maps the plateau itself — what causes it, and what breaks it.

Read together, the four pieces form a cycle: notice the repetition, replace it, then notice the new repetition one level up. That cycle is the whole method, and it is what the interview below unpacks.
